title: Remind before expiry: default by term band and the term cap
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin (Settings Service), on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag). These are numeric/date-accuracy cases (Rule 116): seed the exact inputs, read the produced value back, and compare it to the stated value - never eyeball, never accept "a number".
  2. A compliance service form open (turn on "Is this a compliance inspection?"). Compute each expected value by hand first.
custom_steps:
1. Set the term to 12 months and read the default Remind before expiry.
  2. Set the term to 24 months and read the default Remind before expiry.
  3. With a 6-month term, set Remind before expiry to 6 months, then to 7 months.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Remind before expiry defaults to 1 month for a term up to 12 months (a 12-month term -> 1) and 2 months above that (a 24-month term -> 2).
  • It cannot be longer than the term: with a 6-month term, 6 is accepted and 7 is refused inline ("Remind before expiry cannot be longer than the 6-month term").

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10560 (S3); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S3; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R8: “Remind before expiry ... It is in months, defaults to 1 month for a term up to 12 months and 2 months above that, and can be changed. It cannot be longer than the term; a longer value is refused inline: Remind before expiry cannot be longer than the 6-month term”
